turns.t: Morning, doctor! It's my eye. The left one. It's been watering, nonstop, for about three weeks, and it's driving me up the wall. I'm forever dabbing it.
Tell me more about the watering. Is it worse at certain times?
In the wind, definitely. And when I'm reading. But even indoors, there's always a bit of a tear running down my cheek.
Is the eye red or painful?
No, no pain. It's not red, just wet. Honestly, I look like I'm crying.
Any discharge, or is it sticky in the morning? ~
A tiny bit of crust, now and then. Nothing yellow. ~
Any change in your vision? ~
No, it's the same. ~
Did you have a cold, or any eye infection before this? ~
A cold, in the autumn. And I had my eye tested at the optician, and she said I had a bit of dryness, funnily enough.
Interesting, that can cause watering. What do you do for work?
I'm a taxi driver. Windows down in summer, a lot.
Pulse and temperature, please. ~
Go on. ~
Pulse 72, temperature 36.6.
Fine? ~
Fine. Let me look at the eye. Look up, look down.
Like this? ~
I'm pressing gently on the corner of the eye by the nose. A little fluid comes out the wrong way, and the opening of the tear duct looks narrow.
What does that mean? ~
The tear drains through a tiny channel into your nose. When it's blocked or narrow, the tears have nowhere to go, and they spill over. ~
Blocked? Can that happen? ~
Yes, often with age, or after an infection. I'd say this is a partly blocked tear duct, but I can't rule out dryness of the surface, which also makes the eye water.
What can be done? ~
First, I'd like to arrange for you to see the eye clinic, where they can syringe the duct and check it.
Is it painful? ~
A little uncomfortable, not painful. And in the meantime, massage the corner of the eye gently, downwards towards the nose, a few times a day.
Okay. ~
Use a warm flannel on the eye in the morning, to clear the crusts. ~
Right. ~
I'd like to see you again in four weeks. If it turns red, painful, or swollen at the corner, come back sooner.
Four weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

physical_examination.finding: opening of the tear duct looks narrow

clinical_actions.description: Gentle downward massage at the corner of the eye and a warm flannel in the morning
